items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the education law, in relation to establishing the
"hunger-free campus act"; and making an appropriation therefor
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S1151

SPONSOR: KAPLAN
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the education law, in relation to establishing the
"hunger-free campus act"; and making an appropriation therefor

 
PURPOSE:

This legislation creates the hunger-free campus act, aimed at addressing
food insecurity on public college campuses.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 cites this as the "hunger free campus act" Section 2 states
that the commissioner shall establish the hunger-free campus grant
program. Within amounts appropriated ($10 million) the commissioner
shall award grants on a competitive basis to public institutions of
higher education which are designated by the commissioner as hunger-free
campuses. This funding shall be used to address student hunger, leverage
sustainable solutions to address basic food needs on campus, raise
awareness of services currently offered to address basic food needs,
build partnerships at the local, state and national level to address
food insecurity among students. In order to be designated a hunger-free
campus, an institution shall establish a hunger free task force that
meets at least three times an academic year to set at least two goals
with action plans, designate a staff member responsible with assisting
students with SNAP, provide options for students to utilize SNAP at
campus stores, participate in an awareness day campaign activity and
event during national hunger and homelessness awareness week, provide at
least one physical food pantry on campus or enable students to receive
food through an alternate stigma -free arrangement, develop a program
for free meal vouchers, and annually conduct a student survey on hunger.
Funds shall be allocated to each public institution designated by the
commissioner as a hunger-free campus, in an amount to be determined by
the commissioner. This section also requires a report to be submitted to
the Legislature.

Section 3 appropriates $10 Million.

Section 4 is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

A recent report identified 39% of college students face food insecurity.
The high cost of college tuition can make the ability to afford adequate
meals difficult. Many students are faced with the difficult decision of
whether they should pay their tuition, buy textbooks, pay rent, or
purchase food, a tough decision college students should not have to
make. This legislation aims to address that concern by creating a hunger
task force, designating a staff member as a SNAP point person, making
SNAP more readily accessible on campus, creating campus food pantries,
creating a student meal credit sharing program, as well as creating an
annual student survey on hunger on campus. Already California, New
Jersey, and Minnesota have passed similar legislation.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New Bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

$10 million.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately..
